title: 2026 Semiconductor Industry Market Forecast - Slide Deck & Video Link Available
gist: Future Horizons' Malcolm Penn (reposted by Daniel Nenni) reports August 2026 semiconductor sales crossed a $1tn run-rate with a record 36 straight months of growth, but warns the boom is ASP-driven (90% of dollar growth) and unit growth looks like stockpiling. The text cites a 'revised 2025 forecast now at 125% growth' (likely a typo for 2026) and says non-AI datacentre growth remains mid-single-digit.

insights.claim: Semiconductor sales broke through the $1 trillion barrier in August 2026, per Future Horizons.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Headline confirms an extreme upcycle in chip revenues.
insights.quote: semiconductor sales broke through the $1tn barrier

insights.claim: August 2026 marked 36 consecutive months of month-on-month semiconductor sales growth, the longest sustained growth period in the industry's 70-plus-year history.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Unprecedented cycle length raises mean-reversion risk for semis.
insights.quote: 36 consecutive months of month-on-month growth marked the longest period of sustained growth in the industry’s 70-plus-year history

insights.claim: Future Horizons' revised forecast stands at 125% growth (labelled a 2025 forecast in the text), and the firm warned against 'getting drunk on the numbers'.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Even bullish forecasters are flagging froth; tempers extrapolation of semis growth.
insights.quote: With our revised 2025 forecast now at 125% growth, we warned against getting drunk on the numbers

insights.claim: Future Horizons says the headline semiconductor figures are factual but seriously misleading because growth is concentrated in AI datacentre demand.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Index-level semis strength masks weak breadth; avoid assuming broad-based recovery.
insights.quote: While the figures are factual, they are seriously misleading

insights.claim: Average selling prices accounted for about 90% of semiconductor dollar growth, with ASPs reaching $4.13 in August 2026, 30% above the previous biggest peak.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Price-driven revenue is fragile; an ASP normalization would hit revenues hard (memory especially exposed).
insights.quote: ASPs were responsible for 90% of the dollar growth

insights.claim: Semiconductor unit shipments have returned to growth, but Future Horizons says the growth is not justified by underlying demand and is more likely stockpiling, with another inventory buildup potentially coming.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Inventory build risks a future destocking-driven downturn; watch channel inventories.
insights.quote: more likely the result of stockpiling, with another buildup of inventory potentially on the way

insights.claim: Non-AI datacentre-related semiconductor growth remains in the mid-single digits.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Ex-AI end markets are not booming; favour AI-levered names over broad cyclicals or expect divergence.
insights.quote: non-AI datacentre-related growth still in the mid-single digits

insights.claim: Analogue, discretes and opto segments have stopped declining but have yet to recover.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Analog/power/opto recovery is still ahead; potential laggard trade if cycle broadens.
insights.quote: analogue, discretes and opto yet to recover, although they have now stopped declining

insights.claim: Semiconductor capex as a percentage of chip sales has fallen back below its long-term average trend line.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Lower capex intensity could support supply discipline and future tightness.
insights.quote: Capex spend — tomorrow’s new capacity — as a percentage of chip sales has finally fallen back below the long-term average trend line

insights.claim: Because sales are inflated by ASPs, capex remains high relative to real wafer fab requirements even though capex-to-sales looks below trend.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: The capex-to-sales ratio understates overbuild risk; an ASP reversal would expose excess capacity.
insights.quote: with sales numbers so inflated, capex spend remains high relative to real wafer fab requirements

insights.claim: China is still spending more on semiconductor capex than either Taiwan or Korea.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Chinese capacity build-out is a medium-term oversupply/pricing risk, especially in mature nodes.
insights.quote: China is also still spending more on capex than either Taiwan or Korea
